metadata.title: AI Context Layer - Sources
metadata.description: Primary-source catalog for April 2026 app context-layer architecture: operational truth, memory, retrieval, graph reasoning, grounding, context assembly, knowledge compilation (LLM Wiki pattern), and agent/app integration.

platform_patterns.name: OpenAI - Migrate to Responses
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for stateful context, tool orchestration, and the default OpenAI app runtime surface.

platform_patterns.name: OpenAI - Retrieval
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for retrieval patterns and hosted retrieval guidance.

platform_patterns.name: OpenAI - MCP
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for tool-first and resource-based access over MCP.

platform_patterns.name: Anthropic - Citations
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for evidence-bearing answers and citation-granularity behavior.

platform_patterns.name: Anthropic - Remote MCP Servers
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for live tool and resource integration in Claude-based stacks.

platform_patterns.name: Azure AI Search - RAG Overview
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for Microsoft's current retrieval architecture guidance.

platform_patterns.name: Azure AI Search - Create Knowledge Base
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for managed knowledge-base construction with agentic retrieval.

platform_patterns.name: Google Cloud - Grounding with Vertex AI Search
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for Google-style grounding and retrieval separation.

platform_patterns.name: MCP Specification
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for the MCP protocol that underpins tool-first and resource-based context delivery.

platform_patterns.name: Amazon Bedrock — Embeddings (Nova 2 Multimodal)
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for Amazon Nova 2 Multimodal Embeddings on Bedrock — the AWS-native default embedder for Bedrock Knowledge Bases as of 2026, superseding Titan Embeddings v2. Covers model IDs, supported modalities (text + image), dimension options, and API usage via InvokeModel.

platform_patterns.name: AWS Textract — Developer Guide
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for AWS Textract: S3-event-triggered OCR pipeline handling handwriting, forms, and tables. Used as the AWS-native ingest adapter for regulator PDFs and scanned policy documents in RA11 and policy-and-compliance-docs.md. Pair with Lambda for S3-triggered async pipelines. Standalone Textract is preferred for standardized high-volume doc types; for mixed/variable corpora use Bedrock Data Automation (BDA) which uses Textract as its OCR layer.

platform_patterns.name: AWS Bedrock Data Automation (BDA) — Developer Guide
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for Bedrock Data Automation: AWS-recommended front door for intelligent document processing on mixed or variable document corpora. FM-based classify + extract pipeline (unified March 2026); Textract is the OCR layer inside BDA's 'Bedrock Pipeline' mode. Flat per-doc pricing. Output structured JSON feeds the clause-tree extractor in policy-and-compliance-docs.md. Use standalone Textract for standardized high-volume docs; use BDA for multi-type or unstructured layouts.

platform_patterns.name: Amazon Kendra GenAI Index — Developer Guide
platform_patterns.relevance: Primary source for Amazon Kendra GenAI Index: managed retriever with hybrid + semantic search and a built-in reranker. Index once, reuse across Bedrock Knowledge Bases and Amazon Q Business without dual-indexing. Alternative to self-managed OpenSearch Serverless in AWS Bedrock KB deployments at Tier 3+. Referenced in architectures-by-organization.md (T3 Bedrock KB section) and vendor-landscape.md.

memory_and_context.name: Anthropic - Memory Tool
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for the Anthropic client-side filesystem-as-memory primitive (memory_20250818). Canonical shape for /memories directory, tool commands (view/create/str_replace/insert/delete/rename), path traversal security, and multi-session software development pattern. Verified May 2026.

memory_and_context.name: Anthropic - Claude Opus 4.7 What's New
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for the Opus 4.7 tokenizer change (1.0–1.35× vs Opus 4.6), 1M context window, 128k output, task_budget advisory cap, xhigh effort level, and memory tool improvements. Superseded as the current flagship by Opus 4.8 (May 28 2026) and by the Claude Fable 5 / Claude Mythos 5 / Claude Sonnet 5 lineup (GA June 9–June 30 2026); token-budget and min-cacheable-prefix heuristics derived from any one of these models must be re-measured against whichever model is actually in production — the minimum cacheable prompt length alone ranges from 512 to 4,096 tokens across the current lineup. Verified July 2026.

memory_and_context.name: Anthropic - Introducing Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for the current (July 2026) Anthropic flagship lineup: Claude Fable 5 (GA June 9 2026, briefly export-restricted, restored worldwide July 1 2026) and Claude Mythos 5 (limited release via Project Glasswing). Both ship a 1M-token context window by default and up to 128k output tokens. Anchors current context-window and pricing figures cited elsewhere in this skill; re-verify before treating any specific number as durable, as this lineup has already superseded Opus 4.7/4.8 as the reference flagship within one quarter.

memory_and_context.name: Google Cloud - Agent Engine Memory Bank
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for Memory Bank: exact-match scope dict, IAM conditions on scope, merge-on-write consolidation (created/updated/deleted), memory TTL, immutable revisions with rollback (default revision retention 365 days, verified 2026-10-02), async event processing; advises assuming some sensitive or personal information may still be stored.

memory_and_context.name: Letta - Context Hierarchy
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for explicit context tiers and memory placement decisions.

memory_and_context.name: Letta - Memory Blocks
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for always-visible structured memory blocks and the self-editing memory pattern.

memory_and_context.name: Mem0 - Memory Types
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for episodic, semantic, and user-scoped memory distinctions.

memory_and_context.name: Mem0 - Graph Memory
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for graph-backed memory representations when relationships matter.

memory_and_context.name: LangChain - Context Engineering
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for explicit context design and separation of context surfaces.

memory_and_context.name: LangChain - Long-Term Memory
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for namespaced long-term memory patterns in agent applications.

memory_and_context.name: Zep - Graphiti
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for temporal knowledge graphs with validity windows and real-time incremental updates.

memory_and_context.name: Cognee
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for ontology-based memory and knowledge processing pipelines.

memory_and_context.name: Cloudflare — Introducing Agent Memory
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for Cloudflare Agent Memory (April 2026 private beta): Durable Objects + Workers AI storage, 5-channel parallel retrieval fused with RRF (full-text, exact fact-key, raw message, direct vector, HyDE vector), shared memory profiles across agents, MCP-native, default Llama 4 Scout extraction / Nemotron 3 synthesis. Maps to P2 + P13.

memory_and_context.name: LangMem SDK — LangChain
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for LangMem SDK: background memory manager (auto extraction/consolidation), episodic/semantic/procedural memory tiers (incl. agent self-updating system instructions), prompt-optimization algorithms, MCP-compatible storage. Distinct from LangGraph Store.

memory_and_context.name: Mem0 OSS v3 Migration Guide (v2 to v3)
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for Mem0 OSS v3 (April 2026) architectural change: external graph-database dependency (Neo4j/Memgraph/Kuzu/AGE/Neptune) removed; replaced by built-in entity linking via a parallel `{collection}_entities` store inside the existing vector backend. ~4,000 lines of graph code removed. Graph overlay remains available on the Platform API. Anchors the storage description in vendor-landscape.md.

memory_and_context.name: Mem0 — Token-Efficient Memory Algorithm
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for Mem0 April 2026 single-pass hierarchical extraction algorithm: 93.4% LongMemEval temporal accuracy (vs prior 49.0%), +23.1pt multi-hop improvement, entity linking with semantic+BM25+entity-match fusion. Note: graph relations now influence ranking but are no longer traversable.

memory_and_context.name: Zep v3 — Context Engineering Takes Center Stage
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for Zep v3 rebrand as 'context engineering platform': new ontology (9 node types, 8 relationship types), ISO 8601 temporal queries, 63.8% LongMemEval temporal sub-task / 94.8% DMR (Graphiti v2 figures).

memory_and_context.name: Zep — State of the Art Agent Memory
memory_and_context.relevance: Vendor benchmark post for Graphiti v3 (Zep v3 engine): reports 90.2% LongMemEval / 94.7% LoCoMo at 162ms hybrid retrieval. Figures are as published by vendor — verify before comparing across third-party benchmarks. Prior Graphiti v2 figures (63.8% LongMemEval temporal / 94.8% DMR / P95 ~300ms) appear in the v3 launch post.

memory_and_context.name: Anthropic — New in Claude Managed Agents: dreaming, outcomes, and multiagent orchestration
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for Dreaming as a first-party Claude Managed Agents capability (public beta, May 6 2026): scheduled background process that reviews prior sessions, merges duplicate memories, removes stale entries, surfaces patterns, with human-review gates. Harvey case study reported 6x task-completion improvement. Dreaming is Managed Agents-specific and distinct from the SDK memory tool's /memories directory interface.

memory_and_context.name: Karpathy LLM Wiki v2 (rohitg00 extended writeup)
memory_and_context.relevance: Architectural description of the April 2026 LLM Wiki / knowledge compilation pattern (P7): three-layer system (raw sources → wiki pages → typed schema), ingest-extract-reconcile-supersede pipeline, confidence decay, ingest-time contradiction flags, page types, and provenance classes. Follow-up/extension of Karpathy's original viral post.

memory_and_context.name: Google - Context Engineering: Sessions, Memory (Milam & Gulli)
memory_and_context.relevance: Primary source for the memory source-trust hierarchy (bootstrapped data / user input / tool output), many-to-many memory lineage and regenerate-on-revocation, evolving confidence injected into the prompt, and the system-prompt vs dialogue-history memory injection tradeoff.

memory_and_context.name: Hindsight - repository
memory_and_context.relevance: Open-source agent memory engine: retain/recall/reflect operations, episodes plus facts and entities, evidence-linked observations, multi-leg recall with fusion and rerank. Source for the engine axes table and P21.

memory_and_context.name: Hindsight - documentation
memory_and_context.relevance: Hindsight concepts (memory types, observations, mental models) and self-host versus managed deployment.

memory_and_context.name: Honcho - overview
memory_and_context.relevance: Peer and session memory with background reasoning that derives conclusions; chat endpoint returns synthesised answers. Repository license not verified (repo fetch failed on 2026-10-02).

memory_and_context.name: xmemory - integration overview
memory_and_context.relevance: Schema-driven typed memory: free-text writes resolved into schema-valid objects and relations, structured reads. Only this page was verified; treat other capabilities as unverified.

memory_and_context.name: Supermemory - repository
memory_and_context.relevance: Memory and context API: connectors, fact extraction into a per-entity graph, temporary-fact expiry and conflict resolution, hybrid search.

memory_and_context.name: Supermemory - documentation
memory_and_context.relevance: Supermemory concepts: user profiles, memory versus document RAG, managed and self-hosted deployment.

memory_and_context.name: Claude-Mem - repository
memory_and_context.relevance: Session memory plugin for a coding agent: hook capture, model-written observation summaries, SQLite FTS plus vector index, progressive-disclosure retrieval. No reconciliation or decay documented.

memory_and_context.name: LangMem - repository
memory_and_context.relevance: LangMem source: hot-path memory tools and background memory manager on the LangGraph store.

memory_and_context.name: Mem0 - how it works
memory_and_context.relevance: Mem0 pipeline: add-time extraction and dedup, multi-signal retrieval, explicit update and delete. Graph memory scope differs between platform and open source; check before relying on it.

memory_and_context.name: Mem0 - repository
memory_and_context.relevance: Mem0 open-source library: scoped fact memory with vector and entity storage.

memory_and_context.name: Zep - overview
memory_and_context.relevance: Managed temporal context graph: episodes, fact invalidation with validity times, assembled user context block.

memory_and_context.name: Anthropic - Claude Managed Agents memory
memory_and_context.relevance: Memory stores mounted into the agent filesystem; per-user stores; read-only mounts; dreams write a new store and never modify the input; immutable versions retained 30 days (verified 2026-10-02); redact endpoint; documents the injection-writes-trusted-memory risk.

memory_and_context.name: OpenAI Agents SDK - Sessions
memory_and_context.relevance: Transcript memory keyed by a session ID; get_items/add_items/pop_item/clear_session; SQLite, Redis, SQLAlchemy, Mongo, Dapr, Conversations-API, compaction and encrypted backends; states that a session ID does not authenticate a user and the SQLite backend does not detect edits or replay. The Conversations-API guide was not parsed.

memory_and_context.name: AWS Bedrock AgentCore Memory
memory_and_context.relevance: Immutable CreateEvent short-term memory keyed by actorId/sessionId; async semantic, summary, preference and episodic strategies; hierarchical namespaces with trailing slash and IAM namespace condition keys; eventExpiryDuration covers short-term events only (maximum 365 days, verified 2026-10-02); long-term records need DeleteMemoryRecord or BatchDeleteMemoryRecords.

memory_and_context.name: LangGraph - Persistence and memory store
memory_and_context.relevance: Store namespaces (tuple) plus keys; hot-path vs background writes; profile vs collection trade-off; TTL only through the hosted server configuration.

memory_and_context.name: xmemory - API reference
memory_and_context.relevance: Schema-first typed memory: natural-language and structured writes, scoped writes (reject or drop-and-report), field-level diffs, text-to-SQL reads with return_sql; documents empty-key collapse and silent partial aggregates on scoped reads; lists no history/as-of read, no backfill of new fields, no migration rollback.

memory_and_context.name: xmemory - XMD schema format
memory_and_context.relevance: YAML schema with scalar fields; field descriptions act as extraction guidance; relationships modelled as objects.

memory_and_context.name: xmemory - pricing and deployment
memory_and_context.relevance: Hosted closed engine with open clients; beta-stage design-partner access; no DPA, subprocessor list, or region published at verification time. Re-check before any regulated deployment.

memory_and_context.name: Redis agent-memory-server - repository
memory_and_context.relevance: The open-source server moved to an unmaintained V0 directory; the repo points at a managed offering.

memory_and_context.name: Letta - Agent SDK memory and dreaming
memory_and_context.relevance: Dreaming: background subagents consolidate memory; trigger step-count, compaction-event or off; behavior reminder or auto-launch, fixed at creation; memory lives in MemFS with system/ files in the prompt.

memory_and_context.name: Letta - MemFS
memory_and_context.relevance: Git-backed memory filesystem; every memory edit is a commit; dreaming and memory-doctor subagents edit through git worktrees.

memory_and_context.name: LangMem - Delayed background memory processing
memory_and_context.relevance: ReflectionExecutor debounces memory extraction per thread with after_seconds; local threads end between serverless invocations, so use the remote executor there.

memory_and_context.name: LangMem - reflection.py source
memory_and_context.relevance: Local executor is an in-process worker thread and priority queue over a BaseStore; remote executor creates a delayed LangGraph run with the rollback multitask strategy.

memory_and_context.name: Hindsight - observations
memory_and_context.relevance: Consolidation after retain builds evidence-linked observations; near-duplicate reconciliation within one tag scope, Postgres only; deleting source memories deletes derived observations and re-queues co-sources.

memory_and_context.name: Hindsight - operations API
memory_and_context.relevance: Async work (retain, consolidation, mental-model refresh, graph maintenance) queues as rows in an async_operations table claimed by an in-process or dedicated worker; consolidation is deduped per bank.

memory_and_context.name: Hindsight - configuration
memory_and_context.relevance: Postgres (embedded or external) or Oracle backend; text-search backends native tsvector, vchord, pg_textsearch, pgroonga, pg_search; iterative ANN scan setting.

graph_and_infra.name: Microsoft GraphRAG
graph_and_infra.relevance: Primary source for graph-based retrieval and community-summary style augmentation.

graph_and_infra.name: LlamaIndex - Agent Memory
graph_and_infra.relevance: Primary source for memory organization inside LlamaIndex agents.

graph_and_infra.name: LlamaIndex - Property Graph Index
graph_and_infra.relevance: Primary source for graph-backed retrieval in a modern app stack.

graph_and_infra.name: Supabase AI and Vectors
graph_and_infra.relevance: Primary source for Postgres-native AI, embeddings, and retrieval in app stacks already using Supabase.

graph_and_infra.name: Vercel Agent Resources
graph_and_infra.relevance: Primary source for machine-readable docs and context surfaces exposed to agents.

graph_and_infra.name: Amazon DynamoDB — Developer Guide
graph_and_infra.relevance: Primary source for DynamoDB as the AWS-native session and profile memory store: single-table design with composite keys, TTL for ephemeral session expiry, and on-demand scaling. Used as the P2 structured-memory storage pick on AWS (alongside Postgres).

graph_and_infra.name: paperless-ngx — REST API Documentation
graph_and_infra.relevance: Primary source for paperless-ngx as a self-hosted document-store ingest adapter feeding the personal corpus in RA2 (personal AI). REST API at /api/documents/, consume-folder ingest, built-in OCR. No cloud dependency; pairs with a P8 hybrid index on the local Postgres/SQLite substrate.

graph_and_infra.name: Microsoft GraphRAG - repository
graph_and_infra.relevance: GraphRAG source and status notice. The repository README stated maintenance mode when checked on 2026-10-02; re-check before adopting.

graph_and_infra.name: SQLite - FTS5
graph_and_infra.relevance: Deleted or updated FTS5 entries stay in the index as delete-keys until segments merge unless the secure-delete option (3.42.0+) is set; default off.

graph_and_infra.name: SQLite - PRAGMA secure_delete
graph_and_infra.relevance: secure_delete overwrites freed pages; off by default (compile-time default); needed before deleting personal data from a SQLite memory file.

graph_and_infra.name: pgvector - README
graph_and_infra.relevance: HNSW and IVFFlat apply WHERE filters after the index scan; iterative index scans, partial indexes, and partitioning for selective tenant filters.

graph_and_infra.name: PostgreSQL - Row security policies
graph_and_infra.relevance: Superusers and BYPASSRLS roles always bypass RLS; table owners bypass it unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set.

graph_and_infra.name: Qdrant - Multitenancy
graph_and_infra.relevance: is_tenant payload index for per-tenant filtering inside one collection.

graph_and_infra.name: turbopuffer - architecture
graph_and_infra.relevance: Namespaces as the tenancy unit; eventually consistent reads can be stale.

graph_and_infra.name: Thoughtworks Technology Radar - Crypto-shredding
graph_and_infra.relevance: Per-subject keys destroyed to erase data in backups; placed in Trial. Regulator acceptance not confirmed.

graph_and_infra.name: OWASP LLM08 - Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
graph_and_infra.relevance: Vector-store risks: cross-tenant leakage, embedding inversion, poisoning.

graph_and_infra.name: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
graph_and_infra.relevance: Lists memory and context poisoning (ASI06); title verified only.

graph_and_infra.name: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 on AI models
graph_and_infra.relevance: Addresses AI models, not memory stores; used only as a regulatory anchor.

graph_and_infra.name: Hamburg DPA - discussion paper on LLMs and personal data
graph_and_infra.relevance: Attaches data-subject rights to the input and output of an AI system, naming retrieval-augmented systems.

graph_and_infra.name: Bun - SQLite (bun:sqlite)
graph_and_infra.relevance: Built-in SQLite driver; loadExtension; on macOS Apple's system SQLite omits extension loading, so call Database.setCustomSQLite before opening any database; macOS keeps WAL sidecar files.

graph_and_infra.name: Bun - SQLite build flags
graph_and_infra.relevance: Linux and Windows builds statically link SQLite with SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5; macOS dlopens the system libsqlite3.

graph_and_infra.name: sqlite-vec - JavaScript guide
graph_and_infra.relevance: sqliteVec.load() works with bun:sqlite; macOS may need setCustomSQLite because the built-in SQLite does not allow extensions.

graph_and_infra.name: PostgreSQL - Ranking search results
graph_and_infra.relevance: ts_rank and ts_rank_cd use no corpus-wide statistics, so built-in ranking is not BM25.

graph_and_infra.name: ParadeDB - repository
graph_and_infra.relevance: pg_search: Tantivy-backed BM25 index inside Postgres; community edition AGPL-3.0, enterprise edition commercial.

graph_and_infra.name: VectorChord-bm25 - repository
graph_and_infra.relevance: vchord_bm25 Postgres extension: bm25vector type and Block-WeakAnd index, tokenizers from pg_tokenizer; dual AGPLv3 or ELv2 licence.

graph_and_infra.name: pg_textsearch - repository
graph_and_infra.relevance: Timescale BM25 index for Postgres over text-search configurations; PostgreSQL licence; other WHERE conditions are post-filters under the ordered BM25 scan.

graph_and_infra.name: Neo4j - Vector indexes
graph_and_infra.relevance: Lucene-backed HNSW vector index; filter properties declared in the index and queried with SEARCH ... WHERE.

graph_and_infra.name: Neo4j - Full-text indexes
graph_and_infra.relevance: Lucene full-text index with configurable analyzers and an eventually-consistent option.

graph_and_infra.name: FalkorDB - repository
graph_and_infra.relevance: Property-graph database over sparse adjacency matrices with OpenCypher; SSPLv1 licence; a Graphiti backend.

graph_and_infra.name: Chroma - Full-text search
graph_and_infra.relevance: $contains and $regex document filters; ranked hybrid search with BM25-style sparse vectors and RRF is in the Search API, Chroma Cloud only.

graph_and_infra.name: Chroma - Search API overview
graph_and_infra.relevance: Search API (dense, sparse, hybrid with RRF) is available in Chroma Cloud only.

graph_and_infra.name: Qdrant - Indexing
graph_and_infra.relevance: Payload indexes must exist before ingest for filter-aware HNSW edges, else rebuild; sparse vectors take an idf modifier for BM25-style ranking.

graph_and_infra.name: Qdrant - Hybrid queries
graph_and_infra.relevance: Query API prefetch plus RRF or DBSF fusion of dense and sparse results.

graph_and_infra.name: Milvus - Full text search
graph_and_infra.relevance: BM25 function converts an analysed text field into a sparse vector; hybrid search takes an expr filter per sub-request.

context_engineering.name: Anthropic - Building Effective Agents
context_engineering.relevance: Primary source for context engineering discipline, agent architecture patterns, and context design principles.

context_engineering.name: Anthropic - Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents
context_engineering.relevance: Primary source for the write/select/compress/isolate runtime verbs, context rot, and the canonical context engineering framing adopted in this skill.

context_engineering.name: Drew Breunig - How Long Contexts Fail
context_engineering.relevance: Primary source for the four runtime failure modes (poisoning, distraction, clash, confusion) used as F1-F4 in context-hygiene.md.

context_engineering.name: Drew Breunig - How to Fix Your Context
context_engineering.relevance: Follow-up to 'How Long Contexts Fail' covering mitigations for the four failure modes.

context_engineering.name: OWASP - LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
context_engineering.relevance: Primary source for injection threat model and defenses referenced in security-threat-model.md.

context_engineering.name: Agentic Context Engineering (ACE) — arXiv:2510.04618
context_engineering.relevance: Primary source for P18 ACE pattern (Generator/Reflector/Curator loop, delta updates), A35 context collapse failure mode, and the +10.6% / +8.6% empirical defaults in agent-memory-benchmarks.md.
context_engineering.authors: Zhang, Hu, Upasani, Ma, Hong, Kamanuru, Rainton, Wu, Ji, Li, Thakker, Zou, Olukotun (Stanford + SambaNova + UC Berkeley)

context_engineering.name: Mem0 on LOCOMO — arXiv:2504.19413
context_engineering.relevance: Primary source for the selective-memory vs full-context Pareto numbers (91% lower p95 latency, >90% token cost reduction, +26% LLM-as-Judge vs OpenAI baseline) cited in agent-memory-benchmarks.md.

context_engineering.name: Anthropic Cookbook — Context Engineering: Memory, Compaction, Tool Clearing
context_engineering.relevance: Primary source for compact_20260112 (150K default trigger), memory_20250818 tool (six commands: view/create/str_replace/insert/delete/rename), and clear_tool_uses_20250919 (100K default trigger, keep=3). Anchors P20 AIS, P10 filesystem-as-memory, A37 eager-compaction.

context_engineering.name: Mitchell Hashimoto — Agent = Model + Harness (AI Engineer World's Fair April 2026)
context_engineering.relevance: Primary source for P19 Harness Engineering: the five-column harness model (tool orchestration, verification loops, context & memory, guardrails, observability) and A36 victory-declaration bias. Coined formulation 'Agent = Model + Harness'.

context_engineering.name: Jason Liu — Context Engineering Series Index
context_engineering.relevance: Five-part canonical series on context engineering for agentic RAG. Source for 'agent peripheral vision', faceted search as tool-response design, slash-commands vs subagents, and the 'in-context learning is gradient descent, compaction is momentum' framing relevant to P14 + P20.

context_engineering.name: LangChain — Context Management for Deep Agents
context_engineering.relevance: Industry-standard naming of context-management primitives: offloading large tool results (20K-token threshold), offloading large tool inputs (85% window threshold), summarization fallback. Concrete defaults that complement Anthropic cookbook for non-Anthropic substrates.

research_papers.name: MemoryAgentBench
research_papers.relevance: Four-competency benchmark (Accurate Retrieval, Test-Time Learning, Long-Range Understanding, Conflict Resolution) with EventQA + FactConsolidation datasets. Adds the CR/selective-forgetting axis missing from other benchmarks.

research_papers.name: MemBench
research_papers.relevance: Memory benchmark for LLM-based agents (Tan/Zhang/Ma/Chen/Dai/Dong). Task taxonomy: information extraction, multi-hop reasoning, knowledge updating, preference following, temporal reasoning; factual vs reflective memory levels; participation vs observation scenarios. Cited from the MemBench multi-hop SLO row in agent-memory-benchmarks.md. Previously mis-cited in that file as 2507.05257 (which is MemoryAgentBench) — corrected 2026-05-17.

research_papers.name: LongMemEval-V2
research_papers.relevance: Successor to LongMemEval; web-agent framing with 100M+ token histories; five new axes (static recall, dynamic tracking, workflow knowledge, environment gotchas, premise awareness); AgentRunbook-C baseline 72.5% vs 48.5% RAG.

research_papers.name: Unable to Forget: Proactive Interference in LLM Memory
research_papers.relevance: Empirical study of proactive interference in LLM KV memory stores: accumulating semantically-similar entries suppress recall of the current value; accuracy degrades ~log-linearly; persists regardless of context-window size; resists prompt-engineering mitigations. Motivates F5 in context-hygiene.md.

research_papers.name: Fact Memory vs Long-Context Inference: Cost-Performance Crossover
research_papers.relevance: Directional cost-performance analysis: at 100k-token context, fact-based memory becomes cheaper than long-context inference after ~10 interaction turns. Long-context wins LongMemEval/LoCoMo; fact memory wins PersonaMemv2 and extended-session cost. Uses proprietary baseline — treat as directional criterion, not settled law.

research_papers.name: Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents: A Survey
research_papers.relevance: Background/survey covering memory taxonomy for autonomous agents. Use for orientation and vocabulary; cite primary papers for specific claims.

research_papers.name: Anatomy of Agentic Memory — arXiv:2602.19320
research_papers.relevance: Agentic memory taxonomy and evaluation gaps; covers memory-blindness failure mode and storage-type interaction effects. Grade C preprint — use alongside 2603.07670 for orientation; cite primary papers for specific claims.

research_papers.name: GraphRAG-Bench
research_papers.relevance: Xiao et al. Domain-specific benchmark across 16 disciplines evaluating the full GraphRAG pipeline (construction, retrieval, generation) plus reasoning coherence. Used here for the multi-hop-vs-single-hop routing gate. NOTE: benchmarks GraphRAG variants against BM-25/TF-IDF, NOT against vanilla semantic RAG, and states no multi-hop point gain -- do not quote a pt figure from it.

research_papers.name: When to use Graphs in RAG
research_papers.relevance: The graph-vs-vanilla-RAG comparison GraphRAG-Bench does not make. Reports that 'GraphRAG frequently underperforms vanilla RAG on many real-world tasks' -- the correct source when the claim is about graph losing to flat retrieval.

research_papers.name: LongMemEval — arXiv:2410.10813
research_papers.relevance: Five memory abilities incl. knowledge updates and abstention; synthetic filler; no deletion operator; fact-only values lose information.

research_papers.name: LoCoMo — arXiv:2402.17753
research_papers.relevance: Very long two-speaker conversations; public release smaller than the paper's set; adversarial category without gold answers; no knowledge-update category.

research_papers.name: BEAM — arXiv:2510.27246
